newsitem.title: USA: Democrats relieve fund raising official of duties.
newsitem.headline: Democrats relieve fund raising official of duties.

text.p: The Democratic National Committee has stripped the fund-raising duties of a senior party aide under Republican fire for allegedly soliciting foreign money, a senior party official said on Saturday.

The official, who asked that his name not be used, said the committee has asked the Federal Election Commission to investigate the fund-raising activities of John Huang, a committee vice president for finance.
Huang's fund-raising activities have been sharply critized for links to soliciting money from businessmen with ties to Indonesia, South Korea and other foreign countries.

The official said Huang would devote his time to sorting out the sources of the funds in question. He added that the committee had asked the election commission to investigate the issue on a "fast track" basis so it could be resolved and made public before the Nov. 5 presidential election.

A committee spokeswoman, Amy Weiss Tobe, said Huang "has no current fund-raising assignments" but remained on the committee's staff. She said Huang would fully cooperate with the committee and the election commission in their investigations.
Last month, the committee returned a $250,000 contribution handled by Huang after determining it came from a foreign company, not its U.S. subsidiary.
Republicans were also calling on the party to return $450,000 in contributions from an Indonesian couple, as well as $140,000 raised at a Buddhist temple in California.
The DNC on Friday said it would reimburse the temple $15,000 for the use of its facilities.
